scope: P4-FLOOD-20 semantics; no runtime or public-contract change

generic_fallback.meaning: official flooding/overflow/inundation evidence without a more specific supported flood subtype

flash_flood.meaning: rapid flooding/high-water rise; may be caused by intense rainfall, dam failure, levee failure, ice jam release or other sudden water release

surface_water_flood.meaning: pluvial/surface-water flooding where rainfall exceeds drainage, watercourse or infiltration capacity

debris_flow.meaning: debris/mud/rock-water flow; retained as a distinct hazard even when flood-related

levee_failure.meaning: failure/breach of a levee or dike; a cause/mechanism that can coexist with flood or flash-flood manifestation

dam_failure.meaning: failure/breach of a dam or reservoir structure; a cause/mechanism that can coexist with flood or flash-flood manifestation

glacial_lake_outburst_flood.meaning: sudden drainage/outburst of water impounded by glacier, moraine or ice-related barriers

ice_jam_flood.meaning: flooding associated with river ice accumulation restricting flow; breakup can also trigger downstream flash flooding

contract_relationship.reason: both can carry official flood evidence, but source scope, coverage, family and candidate sets differ
contract_relationship.civil_protection.warning.official: alternate consumer view of official civil-protection sources; does not strengthen source semantics

nina_gap.semantic_rule: unreachable subtype semantics must not be synthesized; design must either add real evidence extraction or narrow the reachable contract

related_distinct_semantics.storm_surge: coastal water-level hazard; not silently collapsed into river/pluvial flood
related_distinct_semantics.coastal_event: coastal/high-surf hazard; not silently collapsed into flood
related_distinct_semantics.debris_flow_in_seismic_contract: same stable hazard type can occur outside the dedicated flood-warning intent; source/contract provenance remains relevant

authoritative_references.source: NOAA/NWS Flood and Flash Flood Definitions
authoritative_references.finding: Flood and flash flood are distinct; flash floods can follow intense rainfall, levee/dam failure or sudden debris/ice-jam releases.
Flash flood is rapid/extreme high water beginning shortly after a causative event.
Ice jam is a stationary accumulation restricting or blocking streamflow.
Glacier-, moraine- and ice-impounded water bodies can drain suddenly with downstream flood consequences.

authoritative_references.source: UK local flood authority guidance - Surface water flooding
authoritative_references.finding: Surface-water/pluvial flooding occurs when rainfall exceeds drainage, watercourse or ground absorption capacity.
GloFAS provides global flood-awareness/model products and is kept distinct from local authority-issued warnings.

invariants: Specific flood subtypes remain distinct from generic flood.
Cause/mechanism and flood manifestation can coexist.
Flood semantic classes are not mutually exclusive when real evidence supports multiple classes.
Heavy rain is not automatically flood or flash flood.
GloFAS model output is not an official warning.
Flood probability is not observed flooding.
Rapid mapping is not automatically an authority-issued warning.
100-year hazard climatology is not a current event.
Storm surge and coastal event remain distinct.
Unreachable NINA GLOF/ice-jam semantics are not synthesized.
Provider ID is not a scoring axis.
Endpoint reachability is not coverage proof.
decisions_for_p4_flood_30: Preserve multiple simultaneous flood subtype semantics additively instead of relying only on one primary hazard_type.
Keep weather.warning.official and natural_hazards.flood.warning as complementary public intents unless a design-level compatibility proof justifies sharing candidates.
Do not route GloFAS raster/model products into official-warning event contracts.
Resolve the NINA GLOF/ice-jam reachability gap using real source evidence only.
Keep heavy-rain weather-warning semantics separate from flood-event semantics.
Reuse alert_stage for official warning events where source data supports it.
